plain_english_policy: Alabama's Ethics Law requires certain public officials and employees to file a Statement of Economic Interests (SOEI) annually. Below is a summary of the categories of individuals who must comply with this requirement for the preceding calendar year, based on the provided text:
policy_direction_if_enacted: The following groups are required to file an SOEI under Alabama's ethics law:
sponsorship_supports_position: The Alabama Ethics Commission oversees this requirement.
evidence_quotes: (1) All elected public officials at the state, county, or municipal level of government and their instrumentalities.
(2) Any person appointed as a public official and any public employee earning $50,000 or more annually.
(3) Candidates for public office from the date they become candidates or file qualifying papers.
(4) Members of the Alabama Ethics Commission; appointed members of boards and commissions with statewide jurisdiction (excluding advisory boards).
(5) Full-time non-merit employees in positions other than maintenance, clerical, secretarial, etc.
(6)-(19) Specific roles such as chief clerks/managers, county administrators, school superintendents/administrators, purchasing agents, directors of state agencies, and more.
(20)-(27) Employees of the Legislature or Judicial Branch in non-maintenance, clerical, secretarial positions.
review_reason: The detailed nature of the information required in the SOEI (e.g., income categories, business ownership details) necessitates human review to ensure accuracy and compliance with Alabama's ethics laws.
